spells/analyze-portal-4986.name: Analyze Portal
spells/analyze-portal-4986.effectSummary: Detects magical portals or gate effects after 1 round of studying an area and reveals their sizes and locations. Once a portal is found, each round of study can reveal, in order, its activation key, special activation circumstances, whether it is one-way or two-way, and then a 1-round glimpse of its destination; each property requires a caster-level check against DC 17 and can be retried on a later round. For unusual portals, a random portal reveals only that it is random and whether it can currently activate; a variable portal reveals only its current destination; a creature-only portal reveals where creatures go but not a separate equipment destination; and a malfunctioning portal reveals only that it malfunctions, not the malfunction type.

provenance.role: primary Expedition to Undermountain catalog record; effect text contains an explicit missing-content marker
complete 3.5 Analyze Portal printing used to restore the omitted unusual-portal mechanics
independent same-spell cross-check for unusual-portal mechanics

spells/anathema-274.name: Anathema
spells/anathema-274.effectSummary: Permanently severs the divine link between the caster's deity and a lower-level cleric, druid, ranger, paladin, or ordinary worshiper of the same faith, even across planes. Affected divine characters lose divine spellcasting and class-granted divine powers such as turning or commanding undead, healing, harming, smiting, shapechanging, and similar abilities. An ordinary worshiper is barred from the faith's services, and a subject who dies under the effect is denied entry to the deity's plane. Members of the faith must shun the subject, while clerics, paladins, druids, and rangers of that faith automatically recognize the anathema by sight. The effect lasts until lifted by the original caster, removed by a higher-level cleric of the same faith using atonement, or ended when the subject changes divine allegiance.

provenance.role: primary catalog record; source prose is silently truncated in the middle of the effect
Champions of Ruin p.28 complete spell text used to restore omitted mechanics

spells/arboreal-transformation-867.name: Arboreal Transformation
spells/arboreal-transformation-867.effectSummary: Transforms the subject into a Huge oak tree. For a number of days equal to caster level, the tree is animated as a treant that cannot animate other trees and serves the caster's commands; it can follow the caster or be left with a triggering phrase as with liveoak. When that duration expires, the subject becomes a normal permanent tree rooted where it stands if possible. A creature that succeeds on its Fortitude save is instead slowed for the spell's duration and returns to normal when that duration ends.

provenance.role: primary catalog record; effect prose is truncated/corrupted at the liveoak reference
complete same-spell 3.5 text used only to restore the omitted mechanics

spells/greater-aspect-of-the-deity-975.name: Aspect of the Deity, Greater
spells/greater-aspect-of-the-deity-975.effectSummary: Functions as lesser aspect of the deity but grants half-celestial or half-fiend qualities without their spell-like abilities, changes the caster's type to outsider for the duration, and still allows resurrection if slain. A good cleric gains feathered wings with flight at twice normal speed and good maneuverability, +1 natural armor, low-light vision, immunity to acid, cold, disease, and electricity, +4 racial on saves against poison, and ability bonuses of +4 Strength, +2 Dexterity, +4 Constitution, +2 Intelligence, +4 Wisdom, and +4 Charisma. An evil cleric gains batlike wings with flight at normal speed and average maneuverability, +1 natural armor, bite and claw attacks based on size, 60-foot darkvision, immunity to poison, resistance 20 to acid, cold, electricity, and fire, and ability bonuses of +4 Strength, +4 Dexterity, +2 Constitution, +4 Intelligence, +4 Wisdom, and +2 Charisma.

spells/blessing-of-the-snake-mother-1380.name: Blessing of the Snake Mother
spells/blessing-of-the-snake-mother-1380.effectSummary: Temporarily grants several yuan-ti tainted-one traits. The target gains the Alertness feat, +2 Constitution, and complete immunity to snake venom and yuan-ti poison. Its appearance becomes more feral and snakelike, and it counts as a yuan-ti for spells and other effects, including favored-enemy interactions and Ghostwalk rules that prevent yuan-ti from forming ghosts. The spell grants the caster no control over the target and is normally used on willing subjects.

spells/celebration-1646.name: Celebration
spells/celebration-1646.effectSummary: Affected creatures receive one Will save when the spell begins. The caster must perform a drinking song for at least 1 full round; intoxication then escalates by performance round: round 1 has no effect, round 2 imposes a -2 enhancement penalty to Dexterity, Intelligence, and Wisdom, round 3 makes the subject nauseated, and round 4 makes the subject helpless. Creatures entering the area after casting are not affected, and affected creatures need not remain in the area. The effects persist while the caster keeps performing; if performance stops, they no longer worsen and fade after 1 round per caster level.

spells/citys-might-3051.name: City's Might
spells/citys-might-3051.effectSummary: While within 100 feet of a qualifying community, grants enhancement bonuses to Strength and Constitution plus damage reduction based on settlement size: large town or smaller +2 Strength/Constitution and DR 2/adamantine; small city +4 and DR 4/adamantine; large city +6 and DR 6/adamantine; metropolis +10 and DR 10/adamantine. If cast more than 100 feet from a community it has no effect, and moving more than 100 feet from the community ends the spell immediately.

Unspent temporary power points disappear after 1 hour.

spells/abyssal-frenzy-1157.effectSummary: Transforms the subject for the duration: land speed +30 feet, +3 enhancement natural armor, +2 profane Strength and Constitution, -2 Dexterity, 60-foot darkvision or +60 feet to existing darkvision, and two claw attacks if it lacked them. spells/crystalline-memories-871.name: Crystalline Memories
spells/crystalline-memories-871.effectSummary: Will negates and spell resistance applies. After casting, the caster must study the target for 3 consecutive rounds, concentrating each round; interruption causes the spell to be lost. When the study completes, the target's current surface thoughts, as detect thoughts, crystallize and erupt from its head, dealing 2d8 damage and 2 Intelligence damage before flying to the caster. Only the caster can spend a full-round action to view the stored thoughts. The crystal lasts 24 hours or until viewed once.

spells/detect-aberration-1529.name: Detect Aberration
spells/detect-aberration-1529.effectSummary: For up to 1 minute per caster level of concentration, the spell scans a 60-foot quarter-circle for aberrant life. Round 1 reveals presence or absence; round 2 reveals the number of aberrant auras and the strongest aura, and an overwhelming aura from a source with Hit Dice or level at least twice your character level stuns you for 1 round and ends the spell; round 3 reveals each aura's strength and location. Aura strength by Hit Dice is 1–3 faint, 4–7 moderate, 8–13 strong, and 14+ overwhelming; a humanoid with Aberration Blood is faint regardless of having more than 3 HD. After a source leaves or is destroyed, its aura lingers for 1d6 minutes if faint, 1d6×10 minutes if moderate, 1d6 hours if strong, or 1d6 days if overwhelming. Each round you can turn to a new area; 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, thin lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt blocks detection.

spells/detect-dragonblood-1056.name: Detect Dragonblood
spells/detect-dragonblood-1056.effectSummary: For up to 10 minutes per caster level of concentration, the spell detects creatures of the dragon type or dragonblood subtype in a 60-foot cone. Round 1 reveals presence or absence; round 2 reveals their number and the strongest aura; round 3 reveals each aura's power and location, or only its direction if outside line of sight. If a detected aura is in line of sight, a Knowledge (arcana) check at DC 10 + the creature's Hit Dice identifies whether it comes from the dragon type or dragonblood subtype. Aura power is: dragonblood subtype—10 HD or lower faint, 11–25 moderate, 26–50 strong, 51+ overwhelming; dragon type—2 HD or lower faint, 3–8 moderate, 9–20 strong, 21+ overwhelming. If more than one category applies, use the stronger aura.

spells/detect-taint-1429.name: Detect Taint
spells/detect-taint-1429.effectSummary: For up to 10 minutes per caster level of concentration, the 60-foot cone detects taint in nearby objects and creatures. Round 1 reveals presence or absence; round 2 reveals the number of tainted creatures and the strongest aura, and if you are free of taint an overwhelming aura at least twice your character level nauseates you for 1 round and ends the spell; round 3 reveals each aura's strength and location, or only its direction if outside line of sight. Aura strength uses the higher of a creature's corruption or depravity score, or the amount of taint bestowed by a source without a taint score: score 1 or 0 taint bestowed is faint; score 2–6 or 1 taint bestowed is moderate; score 7–14 or 1d2/1d3 taint bestowed is strong; score 15+ or 1d4+ taint bestowed is overwhelming. A tainted object or location that bestows no taint is generally faint. Lingering duration is 1d6 minutes for faint, 1d6×10 minutes for moderate, 1d6 hours for strong, and 1d6 days for overwhelming. Each round you can turn to a new area; 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, thin lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt blocks detection.

spells/freeze-armor-1311.name: Freeze Armor
spells/freeze-armor-1311.effectSummary: For 1 round per caster level, metal armor and equipment freeze. Unattended nonmagical metal gets no save; enchanted metal can save, and an item in a creature's possession uses the creature's save if higher. A creature in metal armor that fails its Fortitude save is immobilized, takes -6 on attack rolls and -8 effective Dexterity, cannot move, and must make a Concentration check at DC 15 + spell level to cast; it takes 1d6 cold damage on round 1, 2d6 on round 2, 3d6 on rounds 3–5, and 4d6 on round 6 and later. A metal-armored creature that saves takes half this damage. A creature not wearing metal armor that fails its save takes the listed damage if affected metal it holds, touches, wears, or carries weighs at least one-fifth of its weight; with less metal it instead takes the minimum 1, 2, 3, or 4 points respectively by those same round bands. A creature carrying less than one-fifth its weight in metal that saves is unaffected. Heat damage offsets this cold damage point for point, and vice versa.

provenance.role: primary Frostburn catalog record; prose references a required round/temperature/damage table that is omitted from the rebuilt page
D&D Tools Frostburn SRD copy used only to restore the omitted damage progression table

spells/prismatic-wall-2344.name: Prismatic Wall
spells/prismatic-wall-2344.effectSummary: Creates an immobile vertical opaque wall up to 4 feet wide per caster level and 2 feet high per caster level for 10 minutes per caster level; placing it through an occupied space wastes the spell. The caster can pass or remain nearby safely, but another creature with fewer than 8 HD within 20 feet that looks at it is blinded for 2d4 rounds. Its seven ordered colors are: red—stops nonmagical ranged weapons, deals 20 fire damage (Reflex half), negated by cone of cold; orange—stops magical ranged weapons, deals 40 acid damage (Reflex half), negated by gust of wind; yellow—stops poisons, gases, and petrification, deals 80 electricity damage (Reflex half), negated by disintegrate; green—stops breath weapons, poison kills with Fortitude partial for 1d6 Constitution damage instead, negated by passwall; blue—stops divination and mental attacks, petrifies with Fortitude negates, negated by magic missile; indigo—stops all spells, Will save or become insane as insanity, negated by daylight; violet—destroys all objects and effects and sends creatures to another plane unless they succeed on a Will save, negated by dispel magic. Colors must be removed in order. Rod of cancellation or mage's disjunction destroys the wall; antimagic field does not penetrate it; dispel magic and greater dispel magic cannot dispel the wall or anything beyond it except for the violet layer's listed negation. Spell resistance is checked separately against each color. The wall can be made permanent with permanency.

provenance.role: primary Player's Handbook v.3.5 catalog record; the rebuilt prose loses the seven-color table and contains truncated raw table markup
3.5 SRD reference used only to restore the corrupted seven-color effects and negation table

spells/detect-ship-3339.name: Detect Ship
spells/detect-ship-3339.effectSummary: For 24 hours, you automatically sense other ships within 1 mile per caster level even when they are not visible or you are asleep. For a ship not yet visible, a DC 15 Profession (sailor) check reveals its number, direction, and range; once known, its direction and range remain known while it stays within the spell's range. For a ship within sight, studying it for 1 round allows Profession (sailor) checks that reveal progressively more information: DC 10 type of ship; DC 12 course, speed, and time to intercept if possible; DC 15 weaponry; DC 18 ship name; DC 20 signs of allegiance such as flags or national symbols; DC 25 port of call. The spell cannot penetrate illusions. The arcane focus is a small ground-glass disk on a gold chain worth 50 gp.

provenance.role: primary Stormwrack catalog record; rebuilt prose ends at the introduction to the visible-ship Profession (sailor) results table and omits the table rows
Stormwrack sourcebook rendering used only to restore the omitted Profession (sailor) DC/result table

spells/sandform-3176.name: Sandform
spells/sandform-3176.effectSummary: For 1 minute per caster level, you and all worn or carried equipment become living sand. You take an oozelike form and gain immunity to poison, sleep, paralysis, polymorphing, and stunning; you are not subject to extra damage from critical hits or flanking, but you retain Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma and remain vulnerable to mind-affecting effects. You ignore environmental heat and dehydration but can still take fire and dessication damage. You become blind but gain blindsight 60 feet. Your base attack bonus, base saves, alignment, level, class, hit points, type/subtype, extraordinary abilities, spells, and spell-like abilities remain unchanged; supernatural abilities are suppressed. In demanding situations such as combat, you must make a DC 19 Will save or take -2 on attacks, saves, skill checks, and ability checks until the situation passes. Your land speed becomes 20 feet; you can pass through openings as small as 1/4 inch, though moving through a space at least two size categories smaller takes a full-round action. You gain a pseudopod slam with 5 feet of extra reach; damage by caster size is Fine —, Diminutive 1, Tiny 1d4, Small 1d6, Medium 1d8, Large 2d6, Huge 3d6, Gargantuan 4d6, Colossal 5d6. The number of pseudopod attacks follows your base attack bonus and each adds 1-1/2 times Strength damage; you cannot wield weapons in this form. In sandy terrain you gain a burrow speed equal to your land speed, +10 circumstance on Hide checks, and concealment. On death you revert to your normal form. spells/word-of-balance-3496.name: Word of Balance
spells/word-of-balance-3496.effectSummary: Any lawful good, chaotic good, lawful evil, or chaotic evil creature that hears the word suffers cumulative effects by Hit Dice with no saving throw: HD equal to caster level is nauseated for 1 round; up to caster level -1 is weakened for 2d4 rounds and nauseated; up to caster level -5 is paralyzed for 1d10 minutes, weakened, and nauseated; up to caster level -10 is killed if living or destroyed if undead in addition to the lesser effects. Weakened means -2d6 Strength. Creatures with more Hit Dice than your caster level are unaffected. If you cast on your home plane, aligned elementals and outsiders in the area are also banished to their home plane unless they make a Will save at -4; this banishment does not require them to hear the word, and a banished creature cannot return for at least 24 hours.

spells/summon-undead-i-1460.name: Summon Undead I
spells/summon-undead-i-1460.effectSummary: Functions as summon monster I except that it summons undead. spells/weapon-of-the-deity-1397.name: Weapon of the Deity
spells/weapon-of-the-deity-1397.effectSummary: You must be using your deity's favored weapon. Its full attack is two tentacles +30 for 2d8+14/19–20, six arms +25 for 1d6+7, and bite +25 for 4d6+7. spells/drown-5004.effectSummary: Fills one creature's breathing passages with water for as long as you maintain concentration. spells/enlarge-person-2805.name: Enlarge Person
spells/enlarge-person-2805.effectSummary: Instantly increases one humanoid by one size category, doubling height and multiplying weight by 8. The target gains +2 size Strength, -2 size Dexterity to a minimum of 1, and -1 on attack rolls and Armor Class from increased size; a creature enlarged to Large has 10-foot space and 10-foot natural reach, and speed does not change. If space is insufficient, the creature grows as much as possible and can make a Strength check using its increased Strength to burst the enclosure; failure leaves it constrained without damage, so the spell cannot crush a creature. Worn and carried equipment enlarges too. Enlarged melee and projectile weapons use the larger weapon's damage as applicable, while their other magical properties do not improve. An enlarged item that leaves the creature's possession returns to normal size; thrown weapons therefore deal normal damage, while projectiles deal damage based on the size of the weapon that fired them. spells/evil-weather-139.name: Evil Weather

Violet rain severs connection with divine agencies for 24 hours: divine spellcasters cannot access spells, existing divine spell effects are suppressed, and divinely infused magic items cease functioning; this version additionally costs 10,000 gp in amethysts and 200 XP. Green fog forces living creatures it touches to make Fortitude DC 17 or be polymorphed into a random creature, using reincarnate or an appropriate wilderness list to determine the form. Plague of nettles deals 1d2 damage each round to unsheltered creatures, rapidly destroys crops and forests, and leaves the area infested a week later with dangerous animate plants such as assassin vines, tendriculoses, and shambling mounds. Rain of blood forces living nonevil creatures to make Will DC 20 or take a -1 morale penalty on attack and damage rolls, checks, and saves for 24 hours, while corporeal undead in the rain gain a +1 morale bonus on those rolls for 24 hours. Rain of frogs or fish deals 1d3 damage each round to anyone without shelter, and about one falling animal in twenty survives briefly. Other weather forms have no material component or XP cost. Casting always inflicts the spell's 3d6 Constitution-damage corruption cost.

spells/storm-of-elemental-fury-663.name: Storm of Elemental Fury
spells/storm-of-elemental-fury-663.effectSummary: Creates a 40-foot-radius storm cloud 200 feet above the ground and requires concentration for up to 4 rounds. In the first round, the area below the cloud is a windstorm: unprotected flames are extinguished, protected flames have a 75% chance to go out, normal ranged weapon attacks are impossible, siege-weapon attacks take a -4 penalty, and Listen checks take a -8 penalty. Small or smaller creatures that fail their Fortitude save are blown away; on the ground this knocks them prone, rolls them 1d4×10 feet, and deals 1d4 nonlethal damage per 10 feet. Medium creatures that fail are knocked prone, and Large or larger creatures that fail cannot move that round. Flying creatures that fail are instead blown in a random direction: 1d6×5 feet if Large or larger, 1d6×10 feet if Medium, or 2d6×10 feet if Small or smaller. Spellcasting inside the storm requires a Concentration check against DC equal to this spell's save DC + the level of the spell being cast. Maintaining the spell uses the normal standard action for concentration; as an additional move action you can move the cloud up to 40 feet in any direction. In the second round, falling rock deals 5d6 bludgeoning damage with no save. In the third round, torrential rain extinguishes unprotected flames, has a 50% chance to extinguish protected flames, reduces visibility to 5 feet, and halves movement speed. In the fourth round, flame deals 1d6 fire damage per caster level, with a Reflex save for half; the Complete Divine printing states no damage cap.
spells/storm-of-elemental-fury-663.notes: Repair is locked to the Complete Divine p. 182 printing. Do not import the later Spell Compendium revision, which changes spell level/duration presentation and adds a 15d6 cap.
